stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.focus: Background, timeline, role fit, and process overview.
tips: Prepare a 90-second pitch aligned to Google scale problems.
Confirm interview format (virtual vs onsite) and timezone.
Ask about team matching timing—not compensation details yet.
Be ready to summarize one strong project with metrics.

stages.name: Phone / technical screen
stages.focus: One coding question with strong communication on a shared editor.
tips: Clarify inputs, constraints, and edge cases before coding.
Propose brute force, then optimize; state time/space complexity.
Write clean, testable code; dry-run with a small example.
Google screens often favor medium array/hash/graph questions.

stages.name: Onsite / virtual onsite loop
stages.focus: Mix of coding (2–3), system design (1+ for L4+), and Googleyness/leadership.
tips: Treat each round independently—no carry-over frustration.
Coding: same clarity as phone; expect follow-ups and extensions.
Design: requirements, estimates, APIs, data model, bottlenecks, trade-offs.
Googleyness: STAR stories showing ambiguity, collaboration, and user focus.

stages.name: Team matching / hiring committee
stages.focus: Packet review, level calibration, and team fit conversations.
tips: Stay responsive to recruiters; prepare questions for hiring managers.
Reflect consistent signals: strong coding, communication, and values.
Level discussions weigh scope of past work and interview depth.
Politely compare teams by product impact and growth—not perks alone.

codingTips: Start with examples and invariants; Google interviewers reward structured thinking over fast typing.
Name the pattern (BFS, binary search on answer, interval greedy) out loud—it helps partial credit.
For graphs, state representation (adj list vs matrix) and why before implementing.
When stuck, reduce the problem (smaller input, simpler constraint) and bridge back.
Always propose tests: empty input, single element, duplicates, max constraints.
Prefer readable variable names; Go/Java/Python style clarity matters at Google scale.
If you optimize mid-interview, explain what changed in complexity and why it is correct.
Save 3–5 minutes for follow-ups—they often separate hire vs no-hire at the margin.

eligibility.l3: Typically 0–2 years relevant experience (new grad or early career). Emphasis on coding fundamentals, learning velocity, and collaboration signals.
eligibility.l4: Typically ~2–5+ years. Strong independent delivery, medium/hard coding, and introductory system design on real components.
eligibility.l5plus: Staff+ loops add deep design, cross-team influence, and ambiguous problem ownership. Coding still rigorous but scope questions dominate.
officialQuals: Bachelor’s degree in CS or related field (or equivalent practical experience)—wording varies by posting.
Proficiency in one mainstream language (commonly C++, Java, Python, or Go).
Demonstrated data structures, algorithms, and software engineering experience.
Ability to communicate clearly in English for technical discussions.

disclaimer: Google’s hiring process and rubrics change by region, role, and year. Treat this file as study guidance aligned with public candidate reports—not an official Google document.
